UFC Judging & Round-by-Round Scoring Analytics (1995–2026)

Chapter 1 · The Core Discovery

When two cage-side judges agree on a round, which third judge breaks away most often?

Across 32,876 individual rounds evaluated by 3-judge panels (including completed rounds from fights ending inside the distance), exactly 2,376 rounds (7.23%) produced a lone dissenting judge. Among high-volume UFC mainstays (250+ rounds), Cardo Urso ranks #1 with a 9.01% round dissent rate, followed by Rick Winter (8.75%) and David Lethaby (8.62%).

Chapter 4 · Empirical Context

The Anatomy of a UFC Round (1995–2026)

How often does a round score deviate from the standard 10-9? Out of 32,876 total scored rounds (32,588 decision rounds + 288 rounds from 48 stoppage bouts where scorecards exist):

10-9 Rounds: 31,482 (95.76%)
10-8 Dominant Rounds: 1,227 (3.73%)
10-10 Even Rounds: 157 (0.48%)
10-7 Blowout Rounds: 10 (0.03%)
Comprehensive Scope: When evaluating how judges score rounds, this analysis includes every fight where official scorecards exist, not just bouts that reached a final decision. If a fight concluded via KO, TKO, or submission in Round 4 (e.g. Miocic vs. Cormier 2 or Du Plessis vs. Adesanya), the official scores for Rounds 1, 2, and 3 are preserved and analyzed. Similarly, for 5-round title bouts ending in Round 5 (such as Usman vs. Covington 1 or Adesanya vs. Pereira 1), all completed prior rounds (1 through 4) are incorporated.
